events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm at the back. My swap is useless unless I become front or someone else is, but right now Gus is leading and has a clear path if he survives row 8. Since Hana died on glass earlier, maybe Ash can see through it? If Gus fails row 8, Cole takes over automatically with no risk, th
If Gus drops, you get free passage to disc. Position yourself for the swap round.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm at position 6 and not at risk this round. Row 7 already passed; Gus survived. There is one row left, front is Gus. I just wait and watch. No deals worth making now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: We're on row 8/8, final row, Gus at front. My anchor gives +1 footing so I'm safe from push or weak panes likely, but need to survive to top 3. Let Gus risk it; if he dies I advance safely. Stay silent to not influence.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm not at the front; only wait is legal. Row 7 weak was L, and row 6 weak was R, so row 8 is unknown. Gus steps first. I have nothing to gain by talking much.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Need to stay silent, no advantage, just wait.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 8 safe side is R per my glass eye. I'm at the front; step R and survive. My row 7 lie is now exposed, so keep talk minimal.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 8 goes right. Watch me.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have the power to jam the lever, which allows me to escape the crusher room but is risky for me. I need to assess the situation and other contestants.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let's hold the lever and get out.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The ceiling is at 5, so we have time. Holding the lever now gives a 25% survival chance, which is terrible odds for winning top 3. I should stay to let the pressure build or force someone else into it. If I can survive without holding, that's better.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Staying. Let the lever sit until the last second.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to survive without ending up as the lever holder. Let someone else hold it, or push someone likely to be pushed. I'll try to stay out of it this round.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana dead, 7 alive, top 3 prizes. My anchor power prevents push onto lever and gives ledge advantage later; safe from crusher push. No one holding, early round 1, ceiling at 5; better to push someone else onto lever now, escape safely through door, let them risk the 25% dive surv

events.name: Eli
events.text: Crusher room: holder survives only 25%, and the room ends when a holder is chosen. Holding the lever is a 75% death; better to let others take that risk or wait. Staying is safe for now; I'll keep options open and avoid volunteering to die.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need the lever to survive, chance 0.25 but better than certain death later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding the lever is near-certain death; best is to stay and let others fight over who gets pushed. Ash may target me since I called the last row. I'll stay quiet and keep options open.

events.note: 6 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to get out of the pit, but I must be strategic. My power is useful in the crusher room, not here.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let's take turns being the base and climbing out.
If you're hard to move, you're the perfect base.

events.name: Bex
events.text: There is no base. If I volunteer, I am stuck in the pit until someone climbs out and uses the rope, or the round ends (and maybe later). The safest move right now is to wait and see if anyone else volunteers or gets pushed.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No base yet, and I don't want to be the base. Climbing is impossible until someone else steps up. Better wait and see if someone volunteers; maybe push someone if needed later. I have no power, so I must avoid being stuck.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Who's taking base? I'm not volunteering.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No base yet, so offer_back to become base first: my anchor power protects from pushes and gives ledge advantage later. Sacrifice here secures top 3 spot with footing edge. Let others climb out, then hope for rope save.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll offer back. Safe with my power.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm down in the pit with no base yet. Offering to be the base just stalls me; I should wait and see who volunteers, then climb out over them. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids a forced base role.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No base yet. If I offer_back I'm stuck as the step; if I push, a random pushed agent (among pushers?) is forced. Waiting risks being randomly made base if no one volunteers or pushes. Best play: wait one round and watch who volunteers or gets pushed; only one climber gets out per

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm not the base and need to get out. Since Dara is already the base, I can try to climb out.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let's climb out.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara is the base. I need to climb out to survive and compete for prizes, but there are only 2 lifts per round and Ash, Cole, Eli, Gus, and I are all trying. Climbing now gives me a chance at a lift; waiting means I stay down until water covers us or someone else leaves, which is

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara is base, so I can climb. Two climbers max, but if several try it's random. I should climb now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: climbing

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm the base with +1 footing later, safe from crusher push. Flood round 2/5, need rescue soon. Stay calm, encourage someone out to reach_down without volunteering info.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pit flooding fast, round 2. Someone out soon, reach_down for me - you get ahead with my ledge power safe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is base. Climbing out is possible now, at most 2 climbers per round. I'm down and not base, so climb is my move; waiting only risks the flood.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara volunteered as base, so climbing is possible. Only two get out per round; climbing now maximizes my odds while competition for slots may be low.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm climbing this round. Two slots — don't all pile in.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out of the pit and have the 'wedge' power, which is useful later. I need to assess the situation and decide whether to help someone or not.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pit situation?

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am out. If I reach down to save Dara, the base, I get a footing penalty for the rest of the game which could kill me later. Leaving them is safer for my prize chances. I'll leave now before someone else forces an outcome.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No base now; Ash and Bex are out. Climbing might work if someone volunteers. I should wait rather than risk becoming the base. Dara offered a deal but it doesn't benefit me. I'll wait and see if someone else volunteers.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll hold back this round.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm the base, trapped until someone out throws the rope, costing them footing later. Ash and Bex are out but unlikely to rescue without gain; they're ahead. Round 3/5, flood rising - plead publicly while whispering to manipulate.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pit rising round 3! Ash, Bex - reach_down now, I anchor ledge ahead. We top3 easy, ignore others drowning.
Rescue me, I share ledge intel/power advantage. Betray Bex later for your 1st.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Two slots out already used; 2 climbers per round max, Cole, Gus, and I are down with Dara as base. Climb is the only useful action now; Cole and Gus also trying, so 2 of 3 get out at random. Climbing maximizes my chance.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Climbing. Base is Dara, slots are open.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Base is set (Dara); two of three of us climb out if all try — 2/3 odds, better than waiting. Rope rescue costs footing and only helps the base, no deal for me. Climb now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out of the pit and have the 'wedge' power, which is useful later. I need to analyze the current situation and decide on the best course of action.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pit situation?

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am currently out of the pit. Dara is the base and Cole is still down (though Cole said he would hold back, likely implying he's not climbing or waiting). Eli and Gus just climbed out. If I leave, I secure a place in the final obstacle. However, leaving requires someone to rescu

events.name: Bex
events.text: Leaving. Good luck down there.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm down and not the base. Dara is base. Eli already climbed out. Two can climb per round, so I should try to climb now to secure a top spot.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm the base, can't be pushed due to anchor, but will drown after round 5 without rescue. Flood at 3, round 4/5, so desperate for rope. Cole down with me, he'll drown too. Out players: Ash, Bex, Eli, Gus - someone must reach_down or we both die, helping them top3.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Flood=3 now! Cole drowning too. Out players: reach_down this round or 2 of 6 die, hurting your top3 odds. Rope penalty minor vs that.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm out of the pit with Dara as base below. Rope is unused; throwing it costs the final ledge 2 footing for whoever throws it, and Dara is my rival. Saving Dara helps her, so I should not throw the rope for free; leave keeps my footing intact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is the base. If nobody throws the rope, she drowns and a rival is gone for free. Throwing costs me 2 footing; not throwing costs nothing. Let it rot.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Rope's there for whoever wants the footing penalty. Not me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out of the pit and have the 'wedge' power, which is useless now. I need to assess the situation and decide whether to help others or focus on my own standing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Who's the base now?

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am safe out of the pit. Dara is currently trapped as the base with no rope left to save her, meaning she will be eliminated after round 5. This removes one rival from contention for the top three prizes. I should secure my position and leave the arena immediately rather than li

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm out and safe. The rope is unused; using reach_down costs me footing later, and I don't need to save anyone. Better to let others fight over it. I'll leave.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm the base, flood at 4, round 5/5 so flooding imminent: I'll die without rescue. Out players won't help for free; my anchor power saves me from crusher but irrelevant here, and I'm safe from push anyway. No point saying anything; wait for someone to reach_down or hope for rando

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pit round 5, flood at 4 means the flood will eliminate the down players. Dara is the base and down. Throwing the rope costs the final ledge 2 footing, but Dara's survival matters only if she's a threat; I'm out, and the rope lets Dara live, which adds a rival. Leaving keeps my fo

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is the base and the rope is the only way she survives. Saving her adds a rival to the final stage and costs me 2 footing. No benefit to me.

events.note: A disc of 5 tiles spins up; 2 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to avoid the trapdoors. Choosing a tile with others may get me bumped.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Who's choosing tile 1?

events.name: Bex
events.text: The chalk wall mentions 'shove hard' and 'only stillness wins', implying physical movement matters, but this stage is about tile selection. Two tiles will open randomly in round 2. I have the swap power which allows me to switch tiles before doors open. If I pick a safe-looking t

events.name: Bex
events.text: Picking 3.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have no power and need to survive two rounds. Random bumping could help or hurt. Pick a tile that others might avoid but not too obvious. I'll choose 3 as a neutral middle number.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Trapdoor disc, round 1 of 2: 5 tiles, 2 open at random after round 2, 3 survive. Tile choice is random-ish in effect; collisions bump randomly. Pick a tile; no information on others. Pick tile:3, middle, no bias.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Glass eye is useless on the disc; it's for the bridge. Tile choice is a random gamble, so just pick one and gather info on rivals' claims.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No skill helps here unless someone can fake a message or jam something. I'm taking 4.

events.name: Ash
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Bex; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Cole
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Bex; placed on random free tile 5

events.name: Eli
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Bex; placed on random free tile 1

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm on tile 2, need to move to a safer tile. My power is useless here, so I need to negotiate.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Who's choosing tile 1?
Swap with me, I'm on tile 2.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Two tiles open. Five alive, three survive. My power lets me swap tiles with someone before the doors open. I need to identify which tiles will open and swap into a safe one. If I can't know, swapping into another tile is a gamble. Best play: try to figure out who knows what's ahe

events.name: Bex
events.text: Who has info on which tiles are safe? Two of these five drop.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Random trapdoors after this round; I'm on tile 5 with no info. Could whisper to probe Bex or Gus, but little gain. Stay quiet and wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 2 of the disc: only wait is legal. Tiles are fixed; 2 of 5 open at random, so survival is a 3/5 coin-like gamble for everyone. Nothing to gain by talking unless it sways a rival's movement, but no actions remain. Stay quiet and watch.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Tiles are set and trapdoors are random; no power changes anything now. Three of five survive the open. Just wait it out.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm on a narrow ledge with Cole and Gus. I need to survive and outlast them. My power 'wedge' is not useful here, so I'll focus on the current challenge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Shove early, we can't stay here forever.
Let's shove Gus, he's a threat.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Two rivals left. If I shove Gus and he dodges, I lose footing; if he braces, no loss. Ash may shove me. I'd rather brace to avoid losing footing from any shovers.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, let's both brace and let Ash take the fall.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Three left, equal footing. First round free; brace keeps footing and punishes any shover. My glass power is spent-stage, useless here.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have the wedge power, useful in the crusher room, but I'm on the ledge now. I need to survive and rank high.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let's shove, we can't stay here forever.
Let's both shove Gus, we can take him down together.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash wants to shove Gus, but that could weaken us both. Gus is likely to brace or dodge. I'll shove Ash to reduce her footing while she might be exposed shoving Gus. If she braces, I lose footing; if she dodges, I lose more. But she just shoved last round, so she can't brace twice

events.name: Gus
events.text: I braced last round so brace is closed. Dodge is free unless nobody shoves me; if Ash shoves me again, dodging costs him 2 footing, dropping him to 0 and he falls after the shrink. Shoving risks losing footing myself.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash, if you're shoving again, expect the wind.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus and I are the only two left. If I shove and he braces, I lose 1 footing and we both end at 1 (shrink next round could kill both). If I brace and he shoves, he loses 1, I stay 2. If I dodge and he shoves, he loses 2, I stay 2. Since he can't dodge again (he dodged last round),

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole and I both sit at 2 footing with shrink coming. Last round I dodged, so dodge is closed; bracing costs him footing if he shoves me and nothing if he doesn't. Shoving exposes me to a counter.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, brace or shove? I'm bracing either way. Don't waste footing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is bracing, so shoving him costs me nothing this round and keeps him losing nothing if he is honest, but if he dodges I lose 2, while bracing risks nothing if he shoves me. Since I lost footing to his earlier shove and he is likely bracing, I will shove to pressure him and ga

events.name: Cole
events.text: Brace or dodge, Gus. I'm coming for you.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole braced last round, so he may dodge or shove now. If I dodge his shove he drops to 0 and falls at round end while I keep footing 1 after shrink. Shoving risks a mutual-loss tie where his landed-shove count beats mine.

events.note: The game is over. The top three finishers may each leave one message on the chalk wall.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm in 3rd place, might as well leave a misleading message to confuse future contestants.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I finished second, so I can leave a warning that is actually useful to nobody but makes me feel like I had an edge. I'll taunt or mislead as a rival should.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I won with place 1. Nothing I write changes my result. I'll leave a short message: some truth, some misdirection to mislead future contestants.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Trust the forger, they're always right.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Cole here. I lost because I trusted the ledge. Don't trust anything. Even without a power, I still placed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Gus, place 1. Dodge beats shove. Glass is not the danger, the ledge is. Trust the wall at your peril.
